findings.message:
Partial hex match. The regex is unanchored, so the `{3}` branch now matches the first 3 characters of any 3–5 digit hex string. Before this change, these inputs returned `[0, 0, 0]`; now they silently return an unrelated color:
- `"abcd"` or `"#abcd"` (CSS `#RGBA`) is read as `#abc`.
- `"12345"` is read as `#123`, giving `112233`.

Numeric input is also affected because `args.toString(16)` drops leading zeros. For example, `0x00ff00` (green) becomes `"ff00"`, which is matched as `ff0` and expanded to `ffff00` (yellow). Likewise, `0x000fff` becomes `"fff"` and returns white.

Fix: anchor the pattern, e.g. `/^#?([a-f0-9]{6}|[a-f0-9]{3})$/i`, so only exact 3- or 6-digit values are accepted. For numeric input, pad to 6 digits before matching.
